article_text:
“ Forza ,” Marco Balsamo’s soccer drama shot between Bali and Milan, has been picked up for international sales by EST N8 , which will take the film to the Tokyo International Film Festival ‘s TIFFCOM market (Oct. 28–30). Before that, it gets its first public screening on Oct. 25 at Jakarta Film Week.

Balsamo’s first feature as director centers on Bima, an 11-year-old from Bali who hopes a career as a pro footballer will give his family a better life. A chance bond with a former AC Milan player in the last stretch of his career changes the outlook for both of them.

Related Stories

'Nick Cannon @ Night' Podcast Moves to BET, Will Relaunch as a Weekly TV Talk Show (EXCLUSIVE)

Newcomer Ghazi Alhabsyi heads the cast. Balsamo also appears on screen, alongside Tara Sibel Demren, AC Milan icon Alessandro Costacurta and Atiqah Hasiholan, Oka Antara and Tio Pakusadewo, all three winners at the Indonesian Film Festival (FFI).

Popular on Variety

Balsamo wrote the script and produced with Demren. Riva Studios originated the project, and its producers include Ario Sagantoro of “The Raid” franchise. Adhya Pictures has the film’s Indonesian theatrical release, set for 2027.

Interest at home is strong. Both rounds of online tickets for the Jakarta screening, at CGV Grand Indonesia, sold out inside five minutes.

“‘Forza’ follows a boy from Bali and a former pro footballer who open new doors for each other, and it bridges Indonesia and Italy the way only football can,” said Sophie Shi, head of studios at EST N8. “It’s a film for audiences around the world, with a story of family and hope that transcends language and culture. Our mission is to take bold Asian stories to audiences worldwide, and a family film told through the world’s most popular sport is built to travel. We’re proud to launch ‘Forza’ to buyers at TIFFCOM.”

Shi and Jan Paul Villanueva negotiated the deal for EST N8, with Balsamo and Demren representing Riva Studios. Villanueva, EVP of acquisitions and global distribution, will lead sales with Cathy Ni, head of sales and U.S. distribution, and Shams Pasha, global sales and marketing executive.

“We’ve spent years bringing ‘Forza’ to the screen, and Indonesia has been at the heart of it from the beginning,” Balsamo said. “This film is a labor of love and a testament to the perseverance and collaboration behind independent filmmaking. Sharing the film at Jakarta Film Week is especially meaningful. It’s a moment we’ve been looking forward to for a long time.”

Demren, who co-founded Riva Studios, said the film was designed for families to watch side by side and discuss afterward. “We hope Bima’s journey reminds audiences how much it matters to have someone believe in you, especially when your dreams feel out of reach,” she said. “Seeing both ticket releases fill so quickly is an encouraging start. We’re looking forward to hearing audiences’ reactions.”

Demren and Balsamo set up Riva Studios in 2022 as an independent outfit working in live action, animation and music. In 2024 it bought French animation house TeamTO. “Forza” is its first live-action feature.

Also on EST N8’s TIFFCOM lineup are “Tame,” a Thai horror title from B-EST Pictures; Dean Colin Marcial’s crime thriller “Jaguar,” set in Manila; “Master,” Rezwan Shahriar Sumit’s winner of IFFR’s Big Screen Award; “Pilgrims,” a Korean sci-fi animation from Heo Pyoungkang that was selected for Annecy; and “The Invisible Half,” a J-horror from Nishiyama Masaki.

The company, which brought together EST Studios and N8, has offices in Los Angeles and Bangkok and has sold and distributed more than 60 titles across over 100 territories. Its catalog includes “Hidden Letters,” which was shortlisted for the Oscars and nominated for an Emmy; “The Monk and the Gun,” Bhutan’s Oscar entry; “A Useful Ghost,” which won the Grand Prize at Cannes Critics’ Week; and “Blood Brothers,” which topped Netflix’s global chart.

article_text:
Source: A24

‘The Invite’

The Invite , All Of A Sudden , Clarissa , La Gradiva , and Tender Loving Care lead the way on four nominations each for the 36th edition of The Gothams Film Awards.

Last year The Gotham Film & Media Institute expanded the best feature category from five to 10 slots and the nominees include Club Kid, The Debut, Teenage Sex And Death At Camp Miasma, and Paper Tiger.

Best International Feature nominees include Fatherland, La Gradiva, Possible Love, Minotaur, All Of A Sudden, and Tender Loving Care.

Andrew Scott for Elsinore , Jeon Do-yeon for Possible Love , John Malkovich for Wild Horse Nine , Mahershala Ali for Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother , Julianne Moore for The Debut , and Sophie Okonedo for Clarissa are among the lead performance nominees.

Sandra Hüller garnered a supporting performance nod for Fatherland and goes against Tom Courtenay for Queen At Sea, Penélope Cruz for The Invite, and Kate O’Flynn for Tender Loving Care, among other nominees.

Three years ago the Gothams removed the $35m budget cap on submissions. Netflix’s The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth and The Odyssey were not submitted for consideration before the deadline.

La Bola Negra earned two nominations as Guitarricadelafuente is recognised in the breakthrough performance category, and the film is in the running for the audience award, which returns after an absence of several years, alongside the likes of Obsession and Michael . You Can See Everything i s also in contention for the audience award and best documentary.

The 36th Annual Gotham Film Awards will take place in New York on November 30. Last season One Battle After Another won a sole award for best feature and Jafar Panahi was the star of the ceremony, taking awards for director, screenplay, and international feature. Akinola Davies Jr. won best breakthrough director for My Father’s Shadow.

editorial_title_zh: 罗兰·赖因施塔德勒：《姐妹与阴影》
editorial_excerpt_zh: 这位意大利摄影师在条顿骑士团的隐修院高墙后度过了多年，其作品兼具对日常生活的记述和对他自身天主教成长经历的反思。L’article Roland Reinstadler, Of Sisters and Shadows est apparu en premier sur Blind Magazine .

"translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“人类的灵魂深知阴影，”本书开篇引用的诗句如是承认。条顿骑士团荣誉总团长阿诺德·奥特马尔·威兰（Arnold Othmar Books", "credit": "Blind Magazine", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "罗兰·赖因施塔德勒早在以记者身份在此工作之前，就对这片土地十分熟悉。他在一个两百人的小村庄里长大，从十岁起就在夏天去高山牧场劳作。帕谢尔谷（Passeier Valley）是他家人经营农场的地方，在他的影像中，那里重现了被阳光穿透的乌云，水流“如银子般闪闪发光”。他接受的天主教成长教育构成了这些作品的真正实质：“归根结底，我们如何对待过去，是选择面对还是忽视，完全取决于我们自己。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": Farlow）很早就认可了他的才华。此后，他的影像作品相继发表在《华盛顿邮报》、《明星》周刊以及《明镜》周刊等媒体上。他的第一本著作《Gspell 111》是一幅关于最后几位高山农民之一的肖像，于2022年出版。修道生活有其独特的要求：“这种进入权限绝非理所当然，”他在谈到向他开放拉内格修道院（Lanegg Abbey）的埃伦特劳德·格鲁贝尔修女（Sister Erentraud Gruber）时写道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/roland-reinstadler-9-b3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "© Roland Reinstadler, In "这位摄影师运用当地的光线，光线透过窗户洒落，将房间染红，或在雪地上渐渐消散。一名年轻的求道者面朝下俯卧在地板上，身旁是身着白色长袍的神父，这种伏地致敬代表着“将生命完全奉献给上帝”。在其他地方，一抹红色的微光便足以让十字架沉浸在“一种温暖而又神秘的氛围”中。这本书因此获得了一种严肃的柔和感，而观察者的目光需要花上一小会儿才能辨认出其中的轮廓。", "translated": true}, In Umbra Lucis, GOST Books", "credit": "Blind Magazine", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种虔诚的分量愈发沉重，因为宗教社群的成员正在逐渐减少。一位年迈的修女将手按在胸前，那里有一枚戒指在纪念父母的光芒中闪烁。在泽本修道院（Säben Abbey），十字架散落在木板上，“这是老龄化人口、宗教社群衰落的象征”。修女攀登楼梯的画面——介于黑暗的墙壁与窗户明亮的日光之间——令人感到一种静静的揪心。尽管如此，罗兰·赖因施塔德勒在书的结尾处给出了慰藉：“即便在阴影之中，也依然有着对光明的承诺。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": article_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/roland-reinstadler-19-b2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "© Roland Reinstadler, In Umbra Lucis, GOST Books", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Italian photographer spent years behind the cloister walls of the Teutonic Order, between a chronicle of daily life and a re-examination of his own Catholic upbringing."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "By Guénola Pellen. Photos by Roland Reinstadler ."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/roland-reinstadler-50-b3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "© Roland Reinstadler, In Umbra Lucis, GOST Books", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“The human soul knows shadows,” the poem that opens the book concedes. Arnold Othmar Wieland, Grand Master Emeritus of the Teutonic Order, wrote those lines and has supported Roland Reinstadler’s work since their first conversation. The order grew out of a hospital founded in Acre in 1190 and settled in Bolzano by 1202, before the Pope converted its knights into clerics seven centuries later. Its Austrian-Italian province now has its seat in Lana, among the apple orchards of South Tyrol."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/roland-reinstadler-39-b2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "© Roland Reinstadler, In Umbra Lucis, GOST Books", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/roland-reinstadler-4-b3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "© Roland Reinstadler, In Umbra Lucis, GOST Books", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Roland Reinstadler knew this country long before he worked there as a reporter. He grew up there in a hamlet of two hundred people and spent his summers working an alpine pasture from the age of ten. The Passeier Valley, where his family keeps a farm, returns in his images beneath dark clouds pierced by sunlight, where the water “gleams like silver.” His Catholic upbringing constitutes their real substance: “In the end, it is up to us how we deal with our past, whether we confront it or ignore it.”"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/roland-reinstadler-41-b2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "© Roland Reinstadler, In Umbra Lucis, GOST Books", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/roland-reinstadler-33-b2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "© Roland Reinstadler, In Umbra Lucis, GOST Books", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "He chose to confront it as a self-taught photographer, with a first digital camera bought in 2011. His mentor, the American photographer Melissa Farlow, recognized his talent early. His images have since been published in the Washington Post , Stern and Der Spiegel , among others. His first book, Gspell 111 , a portrait of one of the last mountain farmers, came out in 2022. Monastic life has demands of its own: “This access was anything but a matter of course,” he writes of Sister Erentraud Gruber, who opened Lanegg Abbey to him."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/roland-reinstadler-9-b3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "© Roland Reinstadler, In Umbra Lucis, GOST Books", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/roland-reinstadler-11-b3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "© Roland Reinstadler, In Umbra Lucis, GOST Books", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The photographer works with the light of the place, which falls through a window, reddens a room or fades over the snow. A young candidate lies face down on the floor, priests in white habits at his side, and the prostration represents “the complete surrender of one’s life to God.” Elsewhere a red glow is enough to set a cross in “a warm yet mysterious mood.” The book gains a grave softness from this, and the eye takes a moment to make out the shapes."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/roland-reinstadler-12-b3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "© Roland Reinstadler, In Umbra Lucis, GOST Books", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/roland-reinstadler-53-b2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "© Roland Reinstadler, In Umbra Lucis, GOST Books", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "That devotion weighs all the more because religious communities are gradually losing their members. article_text:
The Italian photographer spent years behind the cloister walls of the Teutonic Order, between a chronicle of daily life and a re-examination of his own Catholic upbringing.

By Guénola Pellen. Photos by Roland Reinstadler .

“The human soul knows shadows,” the poem that opens the book concedes. Arnold Othmar Wieland, Grand Master Emeritus of the Teutonic Order, wrote those lines and has supported Roland Reinstadler’s work since their first conversation. The order grew out of a hospital founded in Acre in 1190 and settled in Bolzano by 1202, before the Pope converted its knights into clerics seven centuries later. Its Austrian-Italian province now has its seat in Lana, among the apple orchards of South Tyrol.

Roland Reinstadler knew this country long before he worked there as a reporter. He grew up there in a hamlet of two hundred people and spent his summers working an alpine pasture from the age of ten. The Passeier Valley, where his family keeps a farm, returns in his images beneath dark clouds pierced by sunlight, where the water “gleams like silver.” His Catholic upbringing constitutes their real substance: “In the end, it is up to us how we deal with our past, whether we confront it or ignore it.”

He chose to confront it as a self-taught photographer, with a first digital camera bought in 2011. His mentor, the American photographer Melissa Farlow, recognized his talent early. His images have since been published in the Washington Post , Stern and Der Spiegel , among others. His first book, Gspell 111 , a portrait of one of the last mountain farmers, came out in 2022. Monastic life has demands of its own: “This access was anything but a matter of course,” he writes of Sister Erentraud Gruber, who opened Lanegg Abbey to him.

The photographer works with the light of the place, which falls through a window, reddens a room or fades over the snow. A young candidate lies face down on the floor, priests in white habits at his side, and the prostration represents “the complete surrender of one’s life to God.” Elsewhere a red glow is enough to set a cross in “a warm yet mysterious mood.” The book gains a grave softness from this, and the eye takes a moment to make out the shapes.

That devotion weighs all the more because religious communities are gradually losing their members. An elderly sister holds a hand against her chest, where a ring shines in memory of her parents. At Säben Abbey, crucifixes lie scattered on a wooden board, “a symbol for an aging population, the decline of religious communities.” The image of a nun climbing a staircase between dark walls and the bright daylight of a window is quietly wrenching. Roland Reinstadler closes his book on a consolation nonetheless: “even in the shadows there is a promise of light.”

In Umbra Lucis by Roland Reinstadler is published by GOST Books .

article_text:
“ You Can See Everything ” audiences were expecting to be taken aback for a variety of reasons when watching the documentary, but a full-frontal shot of Elizabeth Holmes’ partner Billy Evans wasn’t something many foresaw experiencing in the theater. Lance Oppenheim , who co-directed the buzzy A24 doc with Nathan Fielder , has now revealed just how that jarring shower scene came to be — and why Evans might have been fine with revealing all to begin with.

“I honestly don’t know,” Oppnehim said when asked why Evans would agree to appear naked in a recent GQ interview. “It’s beyond me, but I’ve heard interesting theories that people have when they see it,” he said, before getting into the technical details of how they shot it. “There’s a camera in the bathroom, there’s a camera that was on Nathan, there’s a camera outside the bathroom, and there’s an interaction that we see after Billy leaves where he sort of looks at the camera and smiles.”

Popular on Variety

“So I don’t know what that means, but I feel like there’s enough stuff in there that gives me the impression that maybe he was excited that people could see everything and that there was full access, I guess,” Oppenheim continued. “But it really beats me, honestly. We were in the car ride on the way back from the gym, and I said to Billy, ‘We will give you some time to shower.’ And Billy responded, ‘Want to film me showering?’ I offered to film him in a way that could avoid seeing his genitals, but Billy said he didn’t care about being seen naked.”

Ahead of the film’s release earlier this month, Evans admitted he hadn’t seen the doc while appearing on the “All-In” podcast. “I haven’t seen it. I might think this is the dumbest thing I have ever done,” Evans said on the podcast, admitting that Holmes “looks insane” in the trailer.

Before hitting theaters on Oct. 16, “You Can See Everything” had been quietly in the works from Fielder and Oppenheim for more than three years. The doc offers an unhinged look at the Theranos founder a month before she began an 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors.

In addition to being eligible for best documentary feature at the 99th Academy Awards, the film will also be submitted across the board as seen on A24’s awards site: best picture, director, production design, cinematography, costume design, film editing, makeup and hairstyling, sound and original score.

The film has been a major hit with audiences, bringing in $15.6 million from 855 theaters in its opening weekend (the best start for a nonmusical documentary in 20 years) and adding another $19.5 million after expanding to 2,655 venues for its sophomore outing .

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Picturehouse will be releasing the Ari Gold -directed one-shot musical Brother Verses Brother for awards consideration this season.

The movie, touted as a heartbreaking family odyssey through the streets of San Francisco, is executive produced by five-time Oscar winner Francis Ford Coppola , and is inspired by Coppola’s concept of “live cinema.”

Brother Verses Brother follows twin musicians Ari and Ethan Gold as they hunt San Francisco for love, a gig and their dying poet father. As they move from Kerouac Alley through the cafés of the Beats and into the night, they try to finish a new song to play for their father, until Ethan reworks it for the separation that they know is coming. The story, conceived by Ari Gold, is improvised by the director’s own family and friends — including his real father – and Ethan Gold’s songs are performed live on camera as the night unfolds.

Related Stories

2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More

Tokyo Film Festival Chiefs Talk Balancing Blockbusters & Arthouse, Launching International Films In Japan

The song “Brothers Keep Goin’ Anyway” from Ethan Gold has been submitted for Oscar consideration in the Best Original Song category. You can listen to it above.

Watch on Deadline

“Ari and Ethan have created a completely original film with music that fills your heart and makes you long for San Francisco,” Picturehouse CEO Bob Berney said. “We will jump into the awards season immediately with special event screenings and performances and will open the film theatrically early next year.”

“I wanted to make a film about the difficulty of ungluing ourselves from people we love, so an improvisation without cuts was the way,” said Ari Gold. “Our dad agreed to act at age 99, and we discovered that his presence inspires people to bring their own families to the cinema. Bob Berney has spent his career bringing personal films to big audiences, and I can’t think of a better home for our story.”

“I initially wrote ‘Brothers Keep Goin’ Anyway’ in Brother Verses Brother as a ballad for lonely men who don’t know how to love women. It’s for my father and his brothers, and for my brother and myself, about relationships which nurture and curse us. In the film I want my brother Ari to sing it with me to our Dad, but Ari never rehearses, so I change the words and sing it alone as an anthem of freedom for us both, to honor and love each other while breaking our toxic bond,” said Ethan Gold.

Brother Verses Brother also stars Lara Louise, Brian Bell of Weezer, former San Francisco Poet Laureate Tongo Eisen-Martin and literary icon Herbert Gold who at age 99 is in his first and final screen role; one of the last of the Beats, Herbert Gold died eight weeks after filming.

The film is produced by Michelle Stratton, Starr Sutherland, Ari Gold and Scott Feinstein, with Coppola as executive producer. It is a Grack Films production in association with Atypical Project.

article_text:
Critics around the world have hailed the award-winning documentary NAZA as a “brilliant and harrowing” film that is “impossible to ignore”.

NAZA, which is produced by the Guardian and details Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza, was released in UK cinemas this week and will be shown in more than 50 countries. As well as its global cinema releases, NAZA will be available free on the Guardian’s website from late November.

The investigative documentary, which contains 24 interviews with Israeli military insiders speaking anonymously on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, has received widespread praise.

In a five-star review, the Financial Times’s Danny Leigh says that as a piece of cinema, “journalism and film-making brilliantly entwine”. The Times calls the film “hugely provocative and a disturbing account” of Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza, and the Irish Times brands NAZA an “essential record of engineered nightmare”. In a four-star review, the Guardian’s Peter Bradshaw says the “ anguish of Gaza is brought into pin-sharp focus ”.

British Vogue calls NAZA a “brilliant and harrowing film” that outlines the “restrained, meticulous, bone-chilling depiction of the progressive erasure of Gaza”. The magazine says the film “feels destined to become an enduring historical document, one which will and should be seen by generations to come”.

Time Out magazine says NAZA “puts together a restrained, intelligent, articulate, precise and utterly damning case against Israel’s actions in Gaza and their ongoing actions through the region. As a work of cinema, it is exemplary. As a work of journalism, it is inarguable. As a document, it is an indictment.”

The New York Times makes the film a “critic’s choice” and calls NAZA a “haunting” documentary that is “tough to watch, and impossible to ignore”. The Los Angeles Times says NAZA is a “stone-cold frightening” film that “burns the conscience”. And in New York magazine, it is described as “one of the most important films of our time”.

The Hollywood Reporter praises NAZA as a “sober and thoroughly documented bombshell of an exposé” that “leaves one with a deadening feeling, as if humanity may have lost all hope”. The Toronto Star says “NAZA is heartbreaking but essential viewing, questioning the systems that cause and quantify civilian death in modern warfare”.

The Spanish outlet El Mundo hailed NAZA as “the film of our time, a superb, electrifying, and devastating documentary about the systematic model of annihilation of the Palestinian people” that ultimately “points the finger at us. At night, in silence.”

The French newspaper Le Monde says the film “has the effect of an uppercut that leaves the viewer stunned”, while the Danish culture magazine Soundvenue calls NAZA a “soul-crushing testimony to the genocide in Gaza” that is an “example of how the world increasingly seems like a dystopia”.

The United Arab Emirates’ state-owned newspaper the National calls NAZA a “sickeningly tough film to watch”, and an editorial in the Israeli-outlet Haaretz says the film is “trying to force Israelis to confront what they already know: that Israel’s conduct of the war in Gaza has left a black stain”.

When the film opened in Italy last month, it topped the charts . The Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera says NAZA lasts “only 80 minutes, but no more is needed: the ‘scientific’ coldness with which the interviewees reconstruct how they are destroying Gaza is something unforgettable”.

The film contains 24 interviews with Israeli military insiders who detail how an AI-assisted apparatus of mass surveillance was activated during the Gaza war, revealing the systems that were used to target Hamas operatives in the knowledge that large numbers of Palestinian civilians would also die.

Various organisations, including the UN, Amnesty International, B’Tselem and Physicians for Human Rights, the latter two of which are Israeli-based, have said Israel is committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.

The film premiered at the Venice film festival, where it was received a 25-minute standing ovation – a festival record. The documentary went on to win the special jury prize .

editorial_title_zh: 影评 | 《如果我是你3》（Se Eu Fosse Você 3, 2026）：换了一半
editorial_excerpt_zh: 本片将续集寄托于全新的一对情侣，但可预测的幽默和未充分挖掘的冲突限制了其革新的尝试。内容《影评 | 《如果我是你3》（Se Eu Fosse Você 3, 2026）：换了一半》首发于 Cinema com Rapadura 。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "本片将续集寄托于全新的一对情侣，但可预测的幽默和未充分挖掘的冲突限制了其革新的尝试。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "将《如果我是你》中的身体互换交织给新一代，为该系列带来了探索其他婚姻矛盾的可能性。这一前提对于一部关于亲密关系的喜剧而言依然充满活力。然而，《如果我是你 3》正是在塑造这对新情侣的难度上遇到了最大的局限。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "比亚（克莱奥·皮雷斯饰）是克劳迪奥（托尼·拉莫斯饰）和海伦娜（格洛丽亚·皮雷斯饰）的女儿，她是一名主厨，正面临着与极限运动向导阿基里斯（拉斐尔·因凡特饰）的感情危机。是否要孩子成了两人最大的分歧之一，因为他渴望成为父亲，而她则对十七岁时生下的玛丽亚·克拉拉（瓦伦蒂娜·丹尼尔饰）的母亲身份感到满足。当两人神秘地互换身体时，他们也不得不承担起彼此的职业责任。一次美食评审和一场竞技体育比赛，使得他们发现“了解伴侣的日常并不意味着懂得如何去执行”这一事实变得格外尴尬。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "关于生育的分歧为影片提供了一个冲突的机会，因为比亚已经经历过阿基里斯仍在理想化的体验，而生活在对方的身体里本可以使“渴望改变”与“承担其后果”之间的差异变得更加具体。然而，剧本将更多的注意力放在了事务的管理上，而不是这种僵局对这对情侣的揭示上。建立同理心的需求从一开始就指引着剧情，但这些情况的选择显然是为了迎合它们能够顺理成章地引导这种学习过程的便利性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这并不妨碍这部喜剧找到一些精彩的时刻，尤其是拉斐尔·因凡特的表现。这位演员将开头呈现的阿基里斯与后来占据其身体的比亚区分开来，明显地改变了表演的能量。跟随这种转变是一种享受，因为它给人的印象是——尽管剧本没有给予太多支持——一个人正试图在超出其控制的条件下运作。因此，因凡特撑起了那些在纸面上与预期相去甚远的桥段。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "克莱奥则以互补的方向进行创作，通过采取更加散漫和笨拙的姿态来诠释阿基里斯。这种塑造在阿基里斯必须完成他所不擅长的厨房程序的场景中效果最好。在其他时刻，这种角色刻板印象过于依赖传统的男性气概符号。总体而言，影片缺乏对“是什么让比亚和 Aquiles 保持在一起”的更清晰理解，从而无法让这场危机引发兴趣，也无法让未来的和解获得相关性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "美食评论家的评价让比亚把厨房交托给阿基里斯所冒的风险变得显而易见，而阿基里斯缺乏掌控力也引发了两人之间的摩擦。相比之下，极限运动比赛的构建则远没有那么令人信服，未能确立在他职业生涯中处于危险之中的维度的分量。两个环境和职业责任在体验伴侣生活的过程中最终占据了不同的比重。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管厨房和户外活动各自给角色施加了不同的压力，但统一的照明和饱和的色彩拉近了这两个场景的处理方式。总体而言，给人的感觉是这些空间不过是为剧本情境提供的居所。这并不是要求一部身体互换喜剧具备现实主义，而是它缺乏对这些差异的挖掘，从而无法让承担伴侣的工作在视觉上也得到表达。例如，第一部电影中的克劳迪奥的经纪公司和海伦娜的合唱团就处理得要细致得多，它们经过从容不迫的时间铺垫，并为幽默和叙事节奏做出了贡献。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "比亚父母在故事中的短暂出场集中体现了这次革新的另一个问题。作为客串出演，托尼·拉莫斯和格洛丽亚·皮雷斯短暂露面，而前往中国的一次旅行则成为了他们离开的借口。对目的地的肤浅刻画进一步加深了这样一种印象：第二度蜜月（自上一部电影起便被提及）仅仅是为了给这对新情侣让路。这部续集避免沦为对前作的连串致敬，但这个故事几乎没有利用克劳迪奥和海伦娜的经验来推动女儿的成长轨迹。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《如果我是你 3》并不需要复制托尼·拉莫斯和格洛丽亚·皮雷斯的动态来证明其存在的合理性。它需要给这对新情侣一种能够维持兴趣的关系，超越互换身体所带来的尴尬。拉斐尔·因凡特成功地让部分旅程变得有趣，但续集结束时仍未让比亚和阿基里斯成为一对能够唤起人们再次观看渴望的双人组。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "A franquia aposta em um novo casal, mas o humor previsível e os conflitos pouco explorados limitam a tentativa de renovação."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Transferir a troca de corpos de “Se Eu Fosse Você” para uma nova geração oferece à franquia a possibilidade de explorar outros desacordos conjugais. A premissa continua fértil para uma comédia sobre intimidade. Contudo, é na dificuldade de desenvolver esse novo casal que “ Se Eu Fosse Você 3 ” encontra sua maior limitação."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Bia (Cléo Pires), filha de Cláudio (Tony Ramos) e Helena (Glória Pires), trabalha como chefe de cozinha e enfrenta uma crise no relacionamento com Aquiles (Rafael Infante), guia de esportes radicais. A possibilidade de ter filhos se mostra um dos maiores desacordos, pois ele deseja ser pai, enquanto ela se considera satisfeita com a maternidade de Maria Clara (Valentina Daniel), que teve aos dezessete anos. Quando os dois trocam misteriosamente de corpos, precisam assumir também as responsabilidades profissionais um do outro. Uma avaliação gastronômica e uma competição esportiva tornam especialmente inconveniente a descoberta de que conhecer a rotina do parceiro não significa saber executá-la."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "A divergência sobre a maternidade oferece ao filme uma oportunidade de conflito, uma vez que Bia já passou por uma experiência que Aquiles ainda idealiza, e viver no corpo do outro poderia tornar mais concreta a diferença entre desejar uma mudança e arcar com suas consequências. O roteiro, porém, dedica mais atenção à administração dos compromissos do que ao que esse impasse revela sobre o casal. A necessidade de desenvolver empatia orienta a trama desde o início, mas as situações se mostram escolhidas pela facilidade com que podem encaminhar esse aprendizado."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Isso não impede que a comédia encontre alguns bons momentos, sobretudo com Rafael Infante. O ator distingue o Aquiles apresentado no início da Bia que passa a ocupar seu corpo, alterando a energia da interpretação de maneira perceptível. Existe prazer em acompanhar essa mudança porque ela dá a impressão — sem tanto apoio do roteiro — de uma pessoa tentando funcionar sob condições que escapam ao seu controle. Infante sustenta, assim, passagens que, no papel, pouco se afastam do esperado."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Cléo trabalha numa direção complementar, assumindo uma postura mais largada e desajeitada para representar Aquiles. A composição funciona melhor nas cenas em que Aquiles precisa executar procedimentos da cozinha que não domina. Em outros momentos, a caracterização depende demais de sinais convencionais de masculinidade. No conjunto, falta compreender com maior clareza o que mantém Bia e Aquiles juntos, para que a crise desperte interesse e a futura reconciliação também ganhe relevância."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "A avaliação dos críticos gastronômicos torna claro o que Bia arrisca ao deixar a cozinha nas mãos de Aquiles, cuja falta de domínio também provoca atritos entre os dois. Já a competição de esportes radicais recebe uma construção bem menos convincente, sem estabelecer a dimensão do que está em jogo na carreira dele. Os dois ambientes e as responsabilidades profissionais acabam tendo pesos diferentes na experiência de conhecer o parceiro."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "A iluminação uniforme e as cores saturadas aproximam o tratamento da cozinha e das atividades ao ar livre, apesar das diferentes pressões que cada espaço impõe aos personagens. No geral, fica a sensação de que os espaços não passam de acomodações para as situações do roteiro. Não se trata de exigir realismo de uma comédia sobre troca de corpos, mas falta explorar essas diferenças para que assumir o trabalho do parceiro tenha também uma expressão visual. article_text:
A franquia aposta em um novo casal, mas o humor previsível e os conflitos pouco explorados limitam a tentativa de renovação.

Transferir a troca de corpos de “Se Eu Fosse Você” para uma nova geração oferece à franquia a possibilidade de explorar outros desacordos conjugais. A premissa continua fértil para uma comédia sobre intimidade. Contudo, é na dificuldade de desenvolver esse novo casal que “ Se Eu Fosse Você 3 ” encontra sua maior limitação.

Bia (Cléo Pires), filha de Cláudio (Tony Ramos) e Helena (Glória Pires), trabalha como chefe de cozinha e enfrenta uma crise no relacionamento com Aquiles (Rafael Infante), guia de esportes radicais. A possibilidade de ter filhos se mostra um dos maiores desacordos, pois ele deseja ser pai, enquanto ela se considera satisfeita com a maternidade de Maria Clara (Valentina Daniel), que teve aos dezessete anos. Quando os dois trocam misteriosamente de corpos, precisam assumir também as responsabilidades profissionais um do outro. Uma avaliação gastronômica e uma competição esportiva tornam especialmente inconveniente a descoberta de que conhecer a rotina do parceiro não significa saber executá-la.

A divergência sobre a maternidade oferece ao filme uma oportunidade de conflito, uma vez que Bia já passou por uma experiência que Aquiles ainda idealiza, e viver no corpo do outro poderia tornar mais concreta a diferença entre desejar uma mudança e arcar com suas consequências. O roteiro, porém, dedica mais atenção à administração dos compromissos do que ao que esse impasse revela sobre o casal. A necessidade de desenvolver empatia orienta a trama desde o início, mas as situações se mostram escolhidas pela facilidade com que podem encaminhar esse aprendizado.

Isso não impede que a comédia encontre alguns bons momentos, sobretudo com Rafael Infante. O ator distingue o Aquiles apresentado no início da Bia que passa a ocupar seu corpo, alterando a energia da interpretação de maneira perceptível. Existe prazer em acompanhar essa mudança porque ela dá a impressão — sem tanto apoio do roteiro — de uma pessoa tentando funcionar sob condições que escapam ao seu controle. Infante sustenta, assim, passagens que, no papel, pouco se afastam do esperado.

Cléo trabalha numa direção complementar, assumindo uma postura mais largada e desajeitada para representar Aquiles. A composição funciona melhor nas cenas em que Aquiles precisa executar procedimentos da cozinha que não domina. Em outros momentos, a caracterização depende demais de sinais convencionais de masculinidade. No conjunto, falta compreender com maior clareza o que mantém Bia e Aquiles juntos, para que a crise desperte interesse e a futura reconciliação também ganhe relevância.

A avaliação dos críticos gastronômicos torna claro o que Bia arrisca ao deixar a cozinha nas mãos de Aquiles, cuja falta de domínio também provoca atritos entre os dois. Já a competição de esportes radicais recebe uma construção bem menos convincente, sem estabelecer a dimensão do que está em jogo na carreira dele. Os dois ambientes e as responsabilidades profissionais acabam tendo pesos diferentes na experiência de conhecer o parceiro.

A iluminação uniforme e as cores saturadas aproximam o tratamento da cozinha e das atividades ao ar livre, apesar das diferentes pressões que cada espaço impõe aos personagens. No geral, fica a sensação de que os espaços não passam de acomodações para as situações do roteiro. Não se trata de exigir realismo de uma comédia sobre troca de corpos, mas falta explorar essas diferenças para que assumir o trabalho do parceiro tenha também uma expressão visual. Isso foi feito com bem mais cuidado, por exemplo, com a agência de Cláudio e o coral de Helena no primeiro filme, estabelecidos com tempo e calma e contribuindo para o humor e o andamento da narrativa.

A passagem dos pais de Bia pela história acaba concentrando outro problema dessa renovação. Creditados como participações especiais, Tony Ramos e Glória Pires aparecem brevemente, enquanto uma viagem à China justifica seu afastamento. A caracterização superficial do destino reforça a impressão de que a segunda lua de mel (citada desde o longa anterior) serviu apenas para liberar o caminho ao novo casal. A continuação evita se resumir a uma sequência de citações aos filmes anteriores, mas a história pouco aproveita a experiência de Cláudio e Helena na trajetória da filha.

“Se Eu Fosse Você 3” não precisava reproduzir a dinâmica de Tony Ramos e Glória Pires para justificar sua existência. Precisava dar ao novo casal uma relação capaz de sustentar o interesse para além dos constrangimentos da troca. Rafael Infante consegue tornar parte do percurso divertida, mas a continuação termina sem fazer de Bia e Aquiles uma dupla que desperte a mesma vontade de um reencontro.

{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在剧集的语境下，这一场景同样荒诞。霍姆斯的夸张版本并非旨在进行情景再现，不像菲尔德后来在电影中与塞弗里德精心策划的那样。它是一个角色，用于阐释这位行踪不定的科技创始人和已被定罪的骗子的根本本质：她痴迷于改变世界，迫不及待地想要开始，而且——或许最重要的是——她自己也不知道为什么。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这正是《辍学者》的价值、独特性和独创性所在，在经历《你可以看清一切》那令人脑洞大开的直接冲击后，一些观众可能很难体会到这一点。就连在纪录片后半部分作为大众之声和该项目最具价值表演者出场塞弗里德，在目睹霍姆斯观看该剧后，也难以对这部剧进行辩护。当被追问她的表演时，明显感到局促不安的塞弗里德躲在了最简单的解释背后：《辍学者》是一部虚构的电视剧，而她只是在扮演一个角色。", "links": "这倒没错，只是并非全貌。面对一个此前只能在脑海中揣摩演绎的现实，演员感到有些无所适从是可以理解的。（塞弗里德与霍姆斯的几个孩子会面——想必是在母亲不知情的情况下——是电影中最令人尴尬的时刻之一。）但只有在你没看过这部剧的情况下，它才需要辩护；如果你的主要印象来自于电影——其中它被局限于交织在伊丽莎白视角的片段中——而不是来自于在伊丽莎白·梅利韦瑟那部深入剖析、审慎克制且妙趣横生的迷你剧中的第一手体验。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该剧对霍姆斯的诠释是通过事实来审视人物。而电影对霍姆斯的诠释则是直接审视人物以试图揭示事实。两者结合来看，塞弗里德在剧中饰演的这个清晰明确的角色，与霍姆斯在纪录片中可能在扮演、也可能没在扮演的那个极其暧昧模糊的角色并肩而立：既不可捉摸，却又——无论你作何信赖——依然荒诞不经。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在深入探讨之前，先作一个简短的提醒：比较是快乐的窃贼。没有人非得认为《辍学者》比《你可以看清一切》更好，才能认识到两者的艺术成就。在我们这个热衷于盘点榜单、痴迷奖项且往往同质化的娱乐时代，总是习惯于通过宣称某个项目优于另一个来提升其地位，这种肤浅的论调往往只能挑起争议，而无法带来启发。当把电影和电视这两种本就面临文化权力失衡的截然不同媒介联系在一起时，这种做法也尤其显得愚蠢。艺术形式多种多样，且艺术本就具有主观性。因此，让我们不要浪费时间去争论究竟哪种伊丽莎白·霍姆斯的视角更胜一筹。相反，让我们一起来看看它们共同向我们揭示了关于霍姆斯的什么。", "《辍学者》由阿曼达·塞弗里德主演伊丽莎白·霍姆斯，图中显示她正在探望接受化疗的癌症患者并兜售她的假冒医疗设备", "caption": "阿曼达·塞弗里德在《辍学者》中，图片来源：Beth Dubber / Hulu", "credit": "IndieWire", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "text": "《辍学者》的模棱两可较少，但这并不意味着它是定论。是的，该剧将真实事件进行了戏剧化虚构，以讲述一个易于消化、引人入胜的故事。是的，观众看完后会留下这样的印象：伊丽莎白·霍姆斯明知故犯、蓄意为之地通过谎言一路骗取了名誉和财富。《辍学者》中所描绘的欺诈行为是基于事实的，它们在霍姆斯故事中的角色依然重要。而且分量相当重。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部 Hulu 剧集不仅是对启发它的美国广播公司新闻（ABC News）报道的简单回顾。它是极少数拒绝将拍摄对象的动机简化为过去某个变革性瞬间、拒绝归咎于社会弊病、也拒绝将其扁平化为一个邪恶冷酷怪物的传记片。它为未知留出了空间，无论是尚未揭晓的谜底还是人性宏大的不可言说性。虽然纪录片将镜头紧紧锁定在霍姆斯（Holmes）的家中，精妙地复制了与“莉兹”（Liz）共处时的迷人沉浸感，但《辍学生》（The "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "还有她的同行科学家们，他们饱经沧桑的声音指出了霍姆斯为获得 Theranos 资助而跨越的道德底线。（斯蒂芬·弗雷 [Stephen Fry] 的选角堪称精妙——他饰演的伊恩·吉本斯 [Ian Gibbons] 让人心碎如焚，这位首席科学家遭到霍姆斯背叛、解雇、重新聘用，又再次遭到背叛。）还有被她操纵而入局的公司高管，他们的动机既有对其产品所谓利他主义的追求，也有对硅谷科技热潮 FOMO（害怕错漏）心理的推波助澜。（第 4 集标题极其贴切、近乎带有一丝怜悯地叫做《老白男》[Old White Men]。）还有 Theranos 恐吓过的众多专业消息人士以及他们在法庭上穷追猛打的大学生，数十名无辜的人代表了数百万因霍姆斯的公司的行为而受到伤害（其中一些甚至是永久性伤害）的人们。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "霍姆斯在这里自然落了个不好的名声，但这也是她应得的。事实胜于雄辩，正如法庭所证实的那样，她的所作所为正是该剧的焦点。《你无所不见》（You Can See Everything）对发生了什么不感兴趣，它更关心为什么会发生。凭借对霍姆斯的空前近距离接触，菲尔德（Fielder）和奥ppenheim（奥本海默）旨在弄清他们的拍摄对象是否知道自己在说谎（且至今仍在说谎），还是如埃文斯（Evans）的解释所说，她“只是思维方式与众不同”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如果你的印象仅限于她本人——她的故事、她的人生和她的家庭（这些构成了电影的大部分内容），那么霍姆斯就会更容易引发人们的同情。因此，当偶然问到某人是否听说过伊茨abeth·霍姆斯（Elizabeth Holmes）时，他们只是轻描淡写地提到“Hulu 那部剧”，你很容易替她感到沮丧。没有人喜欢被代表，而霍姆斯对自己在《辍学生》（The Dropout）中如何被塑造毫无控制力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这指向了我们文化中的一个更大问题。把一切都娱乐化，从晚间新闻到人们的生活，只会让我们变得更愚蠢。但这并不意味着这部剧本身有问题。几年后，人们在回答同一个问题（“你听说过伊丽莎白·霍姆斯吗？”）时，可能会回答说他们看过“南森·菲尔德（Nathan {"type": "paragraph", "text": "有时，健康的距离能带来更清晰的视角。虽然我不会说这两部作品都对霍姆斯给出了定论，但部分原因在于它们谁也没有声称自己做到了。《辍学生》（The Dropout）和《你无所不见》（You Can See Everything）最终都表明，无论你获得怎样的背景信息——新闻报道、法庭文件、旧日访谈、书籍、电视剧、纪录片——霍姆斯始终是个谜。", article_text:
[Editor’s note: The following article contains spoilers for “ You Can See Everything .”]

Among the snippets of “ The Dropout ” shown in “You Can See Everything,” Amanda Seyfried dancing to “I’m in a Hurry (And Don’t Know Why)” is by far my favorite.

The scene sees Seyfried portraying a 17-year-old Elizabeth Holmes as she stares intently at a poster of Steve Jobs, semi-rhythmically churning her arms and letting herself be seduced by the Apple inventor’s image. As she bends and sways to Alabama’s country-rock classic (in the first of many dance scenes scattered throughout “The Dropout”), it’s as if her ambition is trying to shake free from her body. Her focus shifts, from implicit personal frustrations to an idea sparked by her idol, but it never wavers. She’s determined. Driven. Her famously imposing peepers bulge with excitement.

In the context of the film , the scene is ridiculous. On a computer screen in front of the real Holmes is an exaggerated version of the Theranos founder, who’s watching along with her husband, Billy Evans, and documentarian, Nathan Fielder . When Fielder asks, “Did you really do that?” the answer is a foregone conclusion: Of course she didn’t. And if she did, she would never admit to it now.

In the context of the show, the scene is also ridiculous. The exaggerated version of Holmes isn’t meant to be a reenactment, like what Fielder orchestrates with Seyfried later in the movie. It’s a character, used to illustrate fundamental truths about the elusive tech founder and convicted fraudster: She’s obsessed with changing the world, she can’t wait to get started, and — perhaps most importantly — she doesn’t know why.

Therein lies the merit, the distinction, the ingenuity of “The Dropout,” which some audiences may struggle to recognize in the immediate, mind-bending aftermath of “You Can See Everything.” Even Seyfried, who emerges in the doc’s second half as the voice of the people and the project’s most valuable performer , struggles to defend the show after watching Holmes watch it. When pressed about her portrayal, a visibly rattled Seyfried hides behind the simplest explanation: “The Dropout” is a fictionalized TV show, and she’s playing a character.

That’s true, it’s just not the whole truth. It’s understandable for an actor to be a bit thrown when confronting a reality she’d previously only been able to play out in her head. (Seyfried meeting Holmes’ children, presumably without their mother’s knowledge, is one of the movie’s squirmiest moments.) But the show only needs defending if you haven’t seen it; if your main impression is from the film — where it’s contained to a section enmeshed in Elizabeth’s perspective — and not from first-hand experience within Elizabeth Meriwether’s probing, measured, and gleefully entertaining miniseries.

The show’s take on Holmes depicts the facts to interrogate the person. The movie’s take on Holmes directly interrogates the person to try to uncover the facts. When taken together, the unambiguous character Seyfried plays in the series stands shoulder to shoulder with the very ambiguous character Holmes may or may not be playing in the documentary: unknowable, yet — no matter what you believe — still ridiculous.

Before going any further, a quick reminder: Comparison is the thief of joy. No one needs to believe “The Dropout” is better than “You Can See Everything” to recognize the artistic achievements in both. While it’s always tempting in our list-making, awards-crazed, oft-repetitive entertainment era to elevate one project by claiming its superiority over another, such facile contentions tend to provoke more than they stimulate. They’re also particularly silly when connecting two distinct mediums, like film and TV, which already face a cultural power imbalance. There are many forms of art, and art is subjective. So let’s not waste time fighting over which vision of Elizabeth Holmes is superior. Instead, let’s see what they tell us about Holmes, together.

“The Dropout” never pretends to understand everything about Holmes, and it has that in common with “You Can See Everything.” Despite the documentary’s fanatical quest to determine, as The Atlantic’s David Sims puts it , “whether Holmes is a master manipulator or someone so deeply convinced of her own genius that she can’t distinguish fiction from fact,” Fielder and co-director Lance Oppenheim end up reveling in her inscrutability as well. How we decide what we know about another person’s thoughts and feelings — what we really know — is up to the individual who’s deciding, and what the movie claims to know is decidedly, pointedly torn.

“The Dropout” is less ambiguous, but that doesn’t make it definitive. Yes, the show fictionalizes real events to tell a digestible, entertaining story. And yes, viewers will come away with the impression that Elizabeth Holmes lied her way to fame and fortune, over and over, knowingly and willfully. But the fraud depicted in “The Dropout” is based on the facts, and their role in Holmes’ story still matters. It matters quite a bit.

The Hulu series goes beyond recapping the ABC News reports that inspired it. It’s one of the rare biopics that refuses to reduce its subject’s motivations to a single transformative moment in their past, or place the blame on societal ills, or flatten her into an evil, unfeeling monster. It allows for the unknown, be it a rock that’s yet to be turned over or the grand ineffability of human nature. And while the documentary keeps its tight framing on the Holmes’ household, brilliantly replicating the bewitching immersion of spending time with “Liz,” “The Dropout” takes the same wide lens it gave Holmes and applies it to the sweeping consequences of her crimes.

There’s her fellow scientists, whose experienced voices point out the ethical lines Holmes’ crosses to get Theranos funded. (Stephen Fry is so well-cast — and so searingly heartbroken — as Ian Gibbons, the chief scientist Holmes betrays, fires, rehires, and betrays again.) There’s company executives she manipulates into buying in, motivated as much by the alleged altruism of her product as their own FOMO over the Silicon Valley tech boom. (Episode 4 is perfectly, almost pityingly titled “Old White Men.”) There’s the slew of professional sources Theranos intimidates and the college kids they go after in court, dozens of innocent people who come to represent the millions of people who were hurt, some irreparably, by Holmes’ company.

Holmes, of course, does not come off well here, but she shouldn’t. Actions speak louder than words, and her actions, as proven in court, are the show’s focus. “You Can See Everything” is less interested in what happened than why it happened. With their unprecedented access to Holmes, Fielder and Oppenheim aim to determine if their subject knew she was lying (and still is) or if she “just thinks differently,” to paraphrase Evans’ explanation.

Holmes is much easier to sympathize with if your impression is limited to her — her story, her life, and her family, which make up the bulk of the movie. So when the occasional person is asked if they’ve heard of Elizabeth Holmes and they simply cite “the Hulu show,” it’s easy to feel frustrated on her behalf. No one likes being spoken for, and Holmes had zero control over how she was depicted in “The Dropout.”

That points to a larger problem in our culture. Turning everything into entertainment, from the nightly news to people’s lives, makes us dumber. But it doesn’t mean the show itself is problematic. In a few years, people might respond to the same question (“Have you heard of Elizabeth Holmes?”) by saying they saw “the Nathan Fielder documentary.” Would that mean they’re more informed? More understanding? Does it bring them closer to the truth about Holmes, even when the documentary itself admits the closer we get, the less comprehensible she becomes?

Sometimes a healthy distance provides greater clarity, and while I wouldn’t say either project offers a definitive take on Holmes, that’s partly because neither claims it has. Both “The Dropout” and “You Can See Everything” ultimately contend that no matter what context you’re given — news reports, court documents, old interviews, books, TV shows, documentaries — Holmes remains a mystery.

Which brings us to the question of “characters.” In “You Can See Everything,” Holmes tries to get The New York Times to retract a statement attributed to her about Jennifer Lawrence potentially playing her in a movie: “They’re not playing me,” she said. “They’re playing a character I created.” The implication is Holmes would never admit to creating a character, because that would mean she was conscious of creating a character from the beginning — of putting on a persona to get what she wants. But if she’d done that, then she’d be admitting to knowingly deceiving people, which she can’t admit, since it would be tantamount to acknowledging fraud.

When exposed to her persona — the voice, the black turtleneck, the photo of her holding the tiny vial of blood (which she supposedly hates) — it’s hard to believe what you’re seeing is natural. But the alternative, that she’s been in character in front of every camera that’s ever been thrust in front of her, sounds equally impossible.

“The Dropout” lives in the first belief. It invites the incredulity sparked by Holmes’ bizarre persona through a heightened tone and within Seyfried’s all-in performance. You see her construct the character she’s going to play for the world because you need to see it in order to believe anyone else would believe in this woman and invest in her company. The series lets the facts of what happened provide whatever answers there are regarding Holmes’ inner truth, while using Seyfried’s character as a sometimes legible, sometimes illegible cypher.

“You Can See Everything” is more open to the second belief, or at least starts there, by holding some sympathy for the “real” Holmes. Fielder and Oppenheim don’t set out to make fun of a woman who’s been endlessly mocked for the past decade-plus, and the longer you sit with her, the more possible it feels that she’s been misrepresented and misunderstood all along.

Fielder’s genuine care and consideration extends so much that the film’s final third interrogates if he’s gone too far and can’t see her clearly anymore. After getting as close to her as possible, Fielder still may only be seeing what she wants him to see: the character. Holmes wants him to believe there is no character, that this is just who she is, but he can’t do that. He doesn’t know.

So what does he do? He asks Seyfried for help. He needs a little distance from his subject. He needs to see Holmes from a separate, studied, but still intimate perspective. He needs to see her as Seyfried did in “The Dropout.” It’s helpful, even if it initially seemed like an impediment.

Back in the beach house, when Holmes takes in the scene from “The Dropout” where Seyfried screams “I get the fucking money!” over and over, like a distinctly American wind-up toy, the real Holmes retreats from the screen and cries into pillow. Fielder sits awkwardly at the foot of the bed. Evans offers a reassuring hand. But even in this unmistakably human moment, her motivations are a mystery. Maybe she’s courting sympathy. Maybe she’s genuinely appalled. Maybe she’s simply overwhelmed by competing truths: that she doesn’t see herself in Seyfried’s performance, and that so many other people do.

It made me wonder when Fielder sits down to show Holmes “The Dropout” in the first place, is he giving her space to distinguish the real her from her unwanted public image, as the scene suggests? To refute the “lies” that have defined her until now? To draw the line between the character and the human being?

Or is he forcing Holmes to confront how other people see her? How the world sees her? That, outside of her own unique understanding of reality, there’s another reality where she looks ridiculous, and no one knows why.

“The Dropout” is available on Hulu. “You Can See Everything” is in theaters now.
excerpt_original: Watching Elizabeth Holmes watch "The Dropout" in "You Can See Everything" may leave viewers questioning the merits of Amanda Seyfried's Emmy-winning limited series. But its bona fides are stronger than ever — and the movie knows it.

article_text:
演奏を聞いて、参加して、楽器に触れて…！

人気キャラクター「ガチャピン‧ムック」が出演するファミリー向け体験型コンサート「ガチャピン‧ムックといっしょに！はじめてのクラシック」が11月28(土)、29(日)の両日、東京・お台場のフジテレビ本社で開催されます。

ガチャピン‧ムックは1973年に放送開始した「ひらけ！ポンキッキ」で誕生。以来53年にわたり活躍してきた国民的キャラクターです。今回のコンサートでは、お子様たちがガチャピン・ムックと一緒にクラシックデビュー。プロの演奏を聴いて、一緒に参加して、楽器に触れて…と様々な音楽の体験を楽しむことができます。

会場はフジテレビの球体展望室「はちたま」

さらに会場はフジテレビ本社屋25階の球体展望室「はちたま」の中。特別な空間でお台場の開放的な景色を眺めながらクラシックを楽しみ、ご家族みなさまで元気になれるコンサートです。

ムックのピアノ演奏も聴ける！

またムックと言えば、華麗なピアノの腕前の持ち主としても知られています。ムックのピアノ演奏が聴けるのも本公演の見どころ。公演に向けて、ガチャピンは「みんなといっしょにクラシックを楽しめたらうれしいなあ！！」、ムックは「みなさんの前で演奏するのはとっても緊張しますが、いっぱい練習して挑みますぞ～。」とコメントを寄せています。

龍角散presents ガチャピン‧ムックといっしょに！はじめてのクラシック

ホーム > 作品情報 > 映画「トリコロール 白の愛」

トリコロール 白の愛

劇場公開日： 2026年10月30日

解説・あらすじ

ポーランドの巨匠クシシュトフ・キエシロフスキ監督による、青、白、赤のフランス国旗をモチーフにした三部作「トリコロール」の第2作。 舞台はパリ。性的不能が原因で、妻のドミニクに去られてしまったポーランド人のカロル。故郷へ戻って大金を手にした彼は、どうにかしてドミニカを取り戻そうと策を練る。 主演はズビグニエフ・ザマホフスキー、ジュリー・デルピー。

1994年製作／92分／フランス・ポーランド・スイス合作 原題または英題：Trois couleurs: Blanc 配給：松竹 劇場公開日：2026年10月30日

その他の公開日：1994年8月20日（日本初公開）

フランスはパリ。 ポーランド人のカロル（ヤヌーシュ・ガヨス）は、フランス語は片言しか話せない。 それがゆえかストレスが昂じて、性的不能となり、フランス人の妻ドミニク（ジュリー・デルピー）とは離婚の危機。 というか、裁判で離婚が命じられる。 行き場をなくしたカロルはドミニクに復縁を迫るが、ヒステリー気味の彼女は、こともあろうかふたりが経営している美容室の室内に火を放ち、放火の罪をカロルに着せてしまう。 とうとう行き場をなくしたカロルは、ひょんなことから地下鉄通路で同郷のポーランド人ミコワイ（ズビグニエウ・ザマホフスキ）と出逢い、奇天烈な方法で故郷のポーランドに帰り着き、そこで立派な金満家として成功を収めるが・・・ といった内容で、三部作中唯一のコメディで主役が男性。 カロルがポーランドへ辿り着くまでは好調なんだけれど、彼が成功を収める経緯がぬるく、これだったら元々、成功しているんでないかしらん？などと思ってしまう。 棄てたドミニクへの愛憎ないまぜの復讐劇がはじまり、その復讐の根底には愛があったんだよぉ、というお笑いなんだけれど、キエシロフスキーはどうもコメディ演出は上手くないようで。 本作でも、ガラス瓶の分別箱に瓶を捨てるよぼよぼの老婆が登場しており、『青の愛』の主要人物がちらりと顔をみせます。

天使のような美しいフランス女性と結婚した、ポーランド人のカロル。しかし、性的不能を理由に、妻から離婚を申し立てられる。カロルは妻に未練たらたらだが、妻には冷たくあしらわれ、文無しでポーランドへ帰国。フランスからポーランドへ帰る道のりは、めっちゃ過酷であった。 ポーランドでは、最初兄の家に居候していたが、そのうち成功し、あれよあれよと社長様になった。しっかり財産を築いた後、再婚するでもなく、元妻に復讐(？)を計画する。カロルの計画のため、ポーランドへやって来た元妻ドミニクは、彼の策略通りり、罠にはまってしまう。 ラストでカロルとドミニクが離れた場所から見つめ合い、身振り手振りで語り合いながら涙を流す場面は、本来なら感動的なのだろうが、私は怖かった。カロルの執着が粘着的で、ドミニクの気持ちはそっちのけに思えた。あまり描かれなかったが、ドミニクはカロルを愛していたのか否か。導入部ではこれでもかと冷たくしていたのに、肉体的につながったら態度急変。自分より下に見ていた男が、強く変貌し、性的にも復活したので、つい流されたか負けたんじゃないだろうか。どうも、この男女にはパワーゲームのごとき関係性が見え、それはフランスとポーランドの両国間の格差をダブらせている気がする。カロルはドミニクを征服できたのだろうか。そして、こんな結果に満足できたのだろうか。白い愛とかタイトル付いてて、清らかなイメージだったが、むしろ黒いんじゃね？ BS松竹東急の放送を録画で鑑賞。

article_text:
Nomusa Makhubu on live art, cultural access and reimagining Cape Town through performance

Ahead of the Live Art Festival, ICA Director Professor Nomusa Makhubu speaks with ART AFRICA about the festival’s expansion across Cape Town, from the city centre to KwaLanga, and how live art can engage the city’s spatial histories, broaden cultural access, and create new encounters between art, place, and public life. Official Poster for the ICA Live Art Festival 2026.

Suzette Bell-Roberts: The festival has long worked beyond conventional galleries and theatres. What changes when live art enters streets, public spaces, and heritage sites, and becomes part of the city’s everyday movement?

When live art becomes part of the city’s everyday movement, it makes the intricacies hidden in the rhythms of everyday life perceptible and engages directly with people and how they relate to various parts of the city. The city of Cape Town – loved for its vibrance – bears difficult histories that haunt the city. Live art activates these kinds of contradictions, connecting narratives across time. Collectively walking and experiencing live activations in the city enriches the way we understand it. Image of performance from ICA Live Art Festival 2023. Image courtesy from ICA.

Cape Town remains profoundly shaped by an apartheid spatial geography, with many communities still separated from the city’s established cultural and economic centres. How does this history inform the festival’s decision to work across different parts of the city?

It’s central to our decision and remains one of the ICA’s main concerns. Apartheid spatial geography is a living violence. It limits access to the most basic components of livelihood and liveliness. It limits people’s shared experiences across different parts of the city. It limits freedom of mobility and encumbers meaningful solidarity. We hope that we can contribute to continuing efforts towards multidirectional mobility freedom, create moments for unexpected encounters and convergences, and to have presence in the many existing cultural hubs in Cape Town beyond the CBD.

This year the programme extends into KwaLanga for the first time through partnerships with 16 on Lerotholi and Guga S’Thebe. Why was it important to move beyond the city centre, and what does that shift make possible?

We are excited to be working with 16 on Lerotholi and Guga S’Thebe. 16 on Lerotholi is an incredible platform for the arts and we have deep respect for its founders. It was important for the Live Art festival to move beyond the city centre to forge networks across the city. We recognise that the concentration of cultural institutions in the CBD reinforces imbalances. Most galleries are in the city centre, even though the creative thinking is beyond the city centre. It illuminates the ways in which knowledge circulates. Image of performance from ICA Live Art Festival 2024. Image courtesy from ICA.

The festival is free and open to all. What does meaningful cultural access mean to you, particularly for people who may have had little previous engagement with contemporary or live art?

This is very important to us. This is the kind of festival that should be accessible to everyone and encourage people to engage with the arts. We recognise that the value of creative work is not always monetary. Ours is to try and make it possible for all, regardless of financial means, to enjoy and participate in the arts.

What interests you about audiences who may encounter a work without having deliberately chosen to attend an art event, and how does that change the relationship between artist and public?

Knowledge is produced in the most unexpected places and through unexpected connections. Live art shifts the observer-observed relationship between the public and the artist. In some of the productions, the public can be more than just passive observers (unless, of course, they choose to be). Besides observing, they can participate, co-think, and converse. It is not just a relationship between the artist and the public but also among people interacting. We’re interested in catalysing those moments through incidental encounters between people who intentionally attend and those who serendipitously find and join us. Image of performance from ICA Live Art Festival 2024. Image courtesy from ICA.

Cape Town’s public spaces carry very different histories depending on where one is in the city. How do those histories shape curatorial thinking around site, movement, and performance?

Cape Town’s histories are key to the curatorial process. Histories of enslavement, imperialism, spatial segregation and dispossession overshadow the city and shape today’s social interactions. The curatorial team remained sensitive to this. We approached this festival through an open call and some of the proposals were site-specific, addressing specific histories embedded in place, while others capture the human habits cultivated through those histories. Other works activate the city in various ways by juxtaposing different histories in a given site.

There is a difference between taking a festival into another part of the city and developing a programme that is genuinely shaped by that place. How has the KwaLanga context influenced the festival rather than simply serving as a new venue?

KwaLanga connects histories with it as part of the city (keeping in mind histories of extraction). We start the route from Mendi Avenue to the Beer Hall, 16 on Lerotholi, and Guga S’Thebe, artists revive 20th-century labour histories to show the current impact. We also recognise KwaLanga’s ingenuity in transfiguring those histories. Image of performance from ICA Live Art Festival 2024. Image courtesy from ICA.

Looking at this edition as a whole, what becomes possible when contemporary art is less concentrated in the places where established art audiences already know to look for it?

What becomes possible are fresh perspectives, a rethinking of positionalities and an immediacy between art and the city (art does not merely reflect what is happening but shapes it).

The ICA Live Art Festival 2026 takes place from 14 to 18 October 2026 across Cape Town’s streets, squares, heritage sites, and cultural spaces in the CBD, UCT, and KwaLanga. On Sunday, 18 October, the festival moves through KwaLanga, beginning on Mendi Avenue, continuing to 16 Lerotholi, and concluding at Guga S’Thebe.

article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Peter Medak, the British-Hungarian director of The Changeling, The Krays and Let Him Have It, has died aged 88. According to the Hollywood Reporter, Medak’s family announced he died in Los Angeles on Tuesday.", "links": [{"text": "According to the Hollywood Reporter,", "url": "https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/peter-medak-dead-ruling-class-changeling-1236741708/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Medak enjoyed a long and varied career across film and TV, which included spirit-of-the-times classics A Day in the Death of Joe Egg and The Ruling Class (both from 1972), cult horror The Changeling with George C Scott, and The Krays and Let Him Have It, period true crime films made in the early 1990s. He also directed numerous episodes of high-profile TV drama, including the 80s revival of The Twilight Zone, Homicide: Life on the Street, and Hannibal."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/e79363bd8ab711802ca12f7339bd1bc5bffe3bf5/0_0_3456_2424/master/3456.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "Gary and Martin Kemp as Ronald and Reggie Kray, in dark suits, flank Violet Kray played by Billie Whitelaw in a floral dress", "caption": "Gary Kemp, left with Martin Kemp, right, and Billie Whitelaw in Medak’s biopic of the Kray twins Photograph: Warner Bros./Sportsphoto/Allstar", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Born in Hungary in 1937, Medak escaped the country during the Hungarian uprising and came to London, where his aunt Lotte Medák was an internationally renowned opera singer. Through her contacts Medak was taken on as a trainee at newsreel producers Associated British-Pathé, and worked his way up through the studio departments, including a spell working in the editing room with future Chariots of Fire director Hugh Hudson. Medak then worked as assistant director to Joan Littlewood on Sparrows Can’t Sing and Guy Hamilton on Funeral in Berlin before making his own feature directing debut in 1968 with erotic thriller Negatives, starring Peter McEnery and Glenda Jackson.", "links": [{"text": "taken on as a trainee", "url": "https://www.dga.org/Craft/VisualHistory/Interviews/Peter-Medak"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Medak then followed this up with two adaptations of celebrated plays: Peter Nichols’ A Day in the Death of Joe Egg, with Alan Bates, and Peter Barnes’ The Ruling Class, starring Peter O’Toole. Both were well received on their release in 1972, with O’Toole nominated for the best actor Oscar, but Medak would swiftly hit trouble two years later with Ghost in the Noonday Sun, a still-notorious Peter Sellers vehicle that went vastly over budget, partly due to Sellers’ erratic behaviour, and which was only released on home video more than a decade later. ( Calling it the “biggest disaster of my life” , Medak would later make a documentary about the experience, which screened at the Venice film festival in 2018.)", "links": [{"text": "a still-notorious Peter Sellers vehicle", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/film/2018/aug/11/peter-sellers-spike-milligan-comedy-film-shipwreck-ghost-in-noonday-sun"}, {"text": "Calling it the “biggest disaster of my life”", "url": "https://filmmakermagazine.com/97802-director-peter-medak-plans-to-resurrect-the-ghost-of-peter-sellers/#.W28yNOjdu1s"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Following the Graham Chapman comedy The Odd Job, Medak re-established his credibility with The Changeling, the creepy 1980 George C Scott horror about a composer who rents a haunted house. Calling it “filled with sadness and dread”, it was named by Martin Scorsese as one of his favourite horror movies . After spells on Shelley Duvall’s anthology series Faerie Tale Theatre and The Twilight Zone, Medak returned to features with two high-profile British crime thrillers. The Krays, released in 1990, cast Spandau Ballet’s Gary and Martin Kemp as the twin-brother gangsters, followed by Let Him Have It, about a controversial case which saw 19-year-old Derek Bentley hanged in 1953 for the murder of a policeman despite not pulling the trigger. Medak then returned to Hollywood with the Gary Oldman thriller Romeo Is Bleeding in 1993.", "links": [{"text": "one of his favourite horror movies", "url": "https://www.thedailybeast.com/martin-scorseses-scariest-movies-of-all-time"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/a04f8bca8a14cd1dde1ae8a11cbf18ce273f18d7/0_0_2146_1599/master/2146.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "Peter O'Toole, wig-bearded and in a cream suit, stands smiling with arms outstretched", "caption": "Peter O'Toole in The Ruling Class Photograph: RONALD GRANT", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Medak pivoted back to TV and, starting in 1994, directed six episodes of acclaimed cop series Homicide: Life on the Street, and followed it up by directing an episode of The Wire in 2002. article_text:
Peter Medak, the British-Hungarian director of The Changeling, The Krays and Let Him Have It, has died aged 88. According to the Hollywood Reporter, Medak’s family announced he died in Los Angeles on Tuesday.

Medak enjoyed a long and varied career across film and TV, which included spirit-of-the-times classics A Day in the Death of Joe Egg and The Ruling Class (both from 1972), cult horror The Changeling with George C Scott, and The Krays and Let Him Have It, period true crime films made in the early 1990s. He also directed numerous episodes of high-profile TV drama, including the 80s revival of The Twilight Zone, Homicide: Life on the Street, and Hannibal.

Born in Hungary in 1937, Medak escaped the country during the Hungarian uprising and came to London, where his aunt Lotte Medák was an internationally renowned opera singer. Through her contacts Medak was taken on as a trainee at newsreel producers Associated British-Pathé, and worked his way up through the studio departments, including a spell working in the editing room with future Chariots of Fire director Hugh Hudson. Medak then worked as assistant director to Joan Littlewood on Sparrows Can’t Sing and Guy Hamilton on Funeral in Berlin before making his own feature directing debut in 1968 with erotic thriller Negatives, starring Peter McEnery and Glenda Jackson.

Medak then followed this up with two adaptations of celebrated plays: Peter Nichols’ A Day in the Death of Joe Egg, with Alan Bates, and Peter Barnes’ The Ruling Class, starring Peter O’Toole. Both were well received on their release in 1972, with O’Toole nominated for the best actor Oscar, but Medak would swiftly hit trouble two years later with Ghost in the Noonday Sun, a still-notorious Peter Sellers vehicle that went vastly over budget, partly due to Sellers’ erratic behaviour, and which was only released on home video more than a decade later. ( Calling it the “biggest disaster of my life” , Medak would later make a documentary about the experience, which screened at the Venice film festival in 2018.)

Following the Graham Chapman comedy The Odd Job, Medak re-established his credibility with The Changeling, the creepy 1980 George C Scott horror about a composer who rents a haunted house. Calling it “filled with sadness and dread”, it was named by Martin Scorsese as one of his favourite horror movies . After spells on Shelley Duvall’s anthology series Faerie Tale Theatre and The Twilight Zone, Medak returned to features with two high-profile British crime thrillers. The Krays, released in 1990, cast Spandau Ballet’s Gary and Martin Kemp as the twin-brother gangsters, followed by Let Him Have It, about a controversial case which saw 19-year-old Derek Bentley hanged in 1953 for the murder of a policeman despite not pulling the trigger. Medak then returned to Hollywood with the Gary Oldman thriller Romeo Is Bleeding in 1993.

Medak pivoted back to TV and, starting in 1994, directed six episodes of acclaimed cop series Homicide: Life on the Street, and followed it up by directing an episode of The Wire in 2002. Later TV work included episodes of high-profile shows such as House, Breaking Bad and Cannibal.

Skyfall and No Time to Die writers Neal Purvis and Robert Wade, who worked with Medak on their first produced script Let Him Have It, told the Guardian: “Peter directed our first film and we couldn’t have hoped for a kinder, more respectful collaborator. It was wonderful to be treated as equals by this very experienced film-maker, who was enjoying a resurgence in his film career after the exciting and surprising The Krays. He was a good friend and we will miss the lunches and the talk of all the future projects he still burned to make.”

Medak was married three times, to Katherine La Kermance between 1963 and 1972, Carolyn Seymour between 1973 and 1984, and Julia Migenes between 1988 and 2003.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: English actress Mia McKenna-Bruce ( How to Have Sex ) is the latest to join Throttled , the new Amazon MGM romance based on the first book in Lauren Asher’s Dirty Air series.

Joining the previously announced Nicole Wallace, Josh Heuston, and Julio Peña, McKenna-Bruce plays Sophie Mitchell, the daughter of a powerful figure in the racing world. Sophie is a fan favorite from Asher’s series who leads its second entry, Collided .

Directed by Nzingha Stewart, Throttled centers on Wallace’s Maya Alatorre, an ambitious woman who joins her older brother (Peña) on the Formula One racing circuit and falls into a forbidden, high-stakes romance with his ruthless teammate and fiercest racing rival, Noah Slade (Heuston).

Related Stories

Leslie Bibb Boards Amazon MGM Studios' 'Upgraded 2' Opposite Camila Mendes

Amazon Cornered The YA Market, Now It's Coming For New Adult Stories

Melissa Osborne adapted the screenplay. Max Handelman and Elizabeth Banks of Brownstone Productions are producing along with Ethea Entertainment’s Jennifer Gibgot and Andrew Panay, as well as Garrett Grant. Alison Small of Brownstone and Asher are exec producing. Amazon MGM announced its acquisition of the project for streaming earlier this month.

Watch on Deadline

A BAFTA Rising Star Award winner, McKenna-Bruce broke out with her lead performance in Molly Manning Walker’s critically acclaimed debut feature How to Have Sex , a coming-of-age drama that won the Un Certain Regard prize in its 2023 premiere at Cannes. For her work on the film, released stateside by Mubi, she was honored with the Lead Performance award at the 2023 BIFAs, where she was also nominated for Breakthrough Performance. She was nominated for Best European Actress at the 2023 European Film Awards and won Breakthrough Performer of the Year at the 2024 London Critics’ Circle Film Awards.

Next up, McKenna-Bruce will be seen starring opposite Taron Egerton in the dark comedy Everybody Wants to F*ck Me , which is coming off its TIFF premiere. She also plays Maureen Starkey, the first wife of Barry Keoghan’s Ringo Starr, in Sam Mendes’ upcoming The Beatles – A Four-Film Cinematic Event .

McKenna-Bruce is repped by CAA, 42, Luber Roklin Entertainment, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman.

article_text:
I f you watched this Japanese-language ghost-story horror thriller cold, you might be a little surprised that the credits reveal that the director is one Dave Boyle – and not someone from Japan , so steeped is it in Japanese lore and culture. It turns out that Boyle has been interested in Japan for a long time, and even wrote, directed and starred in the 2006 feature film Big Dreams Little Tokyo, about an American sharing a flat with an aspiring sumo wrestler.

More recently, Boyle was a key director-producer for the Netflix series House of Ninjas, and Never After Dark seems to have evolved as a spun-off side hustle between Boyle and Ninjas star Kento Kaku, who produced it and takes a supporting role.

That all goes a little way to explain how this ends up feeling like a larky, low-stakes, one-for-funsies exercise – inventive and full of charm even if the scares are sort-of predictable.

Shogun ’s Moeka Hoshi stars as Airi, a young woman who looks like a hipster with her torn jeans and raggedy haircut and who travels the country in her Volvo as an itinerant ghostbuster for hire. The ghost of Airi’s dead older sister Miku (Kurumi Inagaki) is always by her side but is only visible in mirrors (as per folklore), and is available to give advice about imminent danger and vibes in the spirit world.

Airi’s latest gig is to exorcise a spirit haunting what used to be a hotel in the sticks. New proprietor Teiko (Tae Kimura) has been hearing bumps in the night and getting creepy phone calls that are either from spirits or perverts, or possibly both. Teiko’s son Gunji (Kaku) is less convinced there’s a supernatural explanation but he takes a shine to Airi all the same, especially when it is revealed that they share a taste for niche music.

Soon Airi works out that the apparition wandering the corridors and scrabbling at the wainscoting is a man with a gruesomely smashed jaw (Mutsuo Yoshioka), and she can interact with him on the astral plane via a ritual involving a candle, burnt offerings of her own hair (thus the shaggy hairstyle), and a phenakistoscope, a 19th-century persistence-of-vision toy , which in this case depicts a spirit rising from a body. But getting the smashed-mouth spirit out of the house proves to be anything but the run-of-the-mill exorcism Airi expected.

Boyle and his collaborators deploy charmingly old-school physical effects, the sort of thing actual phenakistoscope users might have been impressed by in films by the likes of Georges Méliès . It’s mostly a matter of camera angles capturing faces in mirrors and reflections, wire work and well choreographed use of body doubles. The old school vibe makes this particularly endearing, even if the characterisation isn’t especially complex or nuanced, but Hoshi brings a spontaneity and intelligence to the lead role that is consistently winning.

article_text:
国立新美術館（東京都港区）で開催中の「ルーヴル美術館展 ルネサンス」。 Yteen美術部では、この展覧会の無料観覧券を5組10名（中高生とその保護者対象）にプレゼント。

ルネサンスは、古代ギリシア・ローマにならって人間中心の文化をつくろうとした動きで、15~16世紀のヨーロッパで大きく花開きました。展覧会では「旅」「技法の革新と洗練」「古代へのまなざし」「肖像芸術の隆盛」という四つのテーマから、ルネサンスの魅力に迫ります。

会場には、フランス・パリのルーヴル美術館が所蔵する絵画や彫刻、版画、素描、工芸なと56点が並んでいます。最大の注目は、レオナルド・ダ・ヴィンチの《女性の肖像》、通称《美しきフェロニエール》。日本で展示されるのは初めてになります。レオナルドの真筆とされる絵画は世界にわずか15点ほどしかなく、ルーヴル美術館が所蔵する彼の作品が日本にやって来るのは、1974年の《モナ・リザ》以来、実に半世紀ぶりです。

展覧会は12月13日まで。

＊申し込みは 10月30日（金） まで。 当選者は5組10名で、中高生とその保護者が対象となります。（中高生以外の方のみの応募はできません） 応募者多数の場合は抽選となります。

読売IDでログイン後、アンケートに回答していただくことで応募することができます。 アンケートはログイン後のページ下部に表示されます。

※読売IDをお持ちでない方は、下記「会員登録」ボタンより会員登録を行う必要がございます。どなたでも無料でご登録いただけます。 ※応募はお一人様１回限りとさせていただきます。 ※プレゼントのお届けには住所登録が必要です。住所の登録がない方には発送できませんのでご注意ください。

当選者の発表は発送をもってかえさせていただきます。

以降の記事は会員専用となります。会員の方はログインして続きを御覧ください。 会員登録がお済みでない方は会員登録をお願い致します。

article_text:
ヤマトよ永遠に REBEL3199 第七章 虹色の輪廻

劇場公開日： 2026年10月30日

解説・あらすじ

名作アニメ「宇宙戦艦ヤマト」のリメイクシリーズの1作で、1980年公開の劇場映画第3作「ヤマトよ永遠（とわ）に」とテレビアニメ第3作「宇宙戦艦ヤマトIII」に新たな解釈を加えて再構成した「ヤマトよ永遠に REBEL3199」全7章（全26話）の最終章となる第7章。 これまで信じてきた現実が崩れ、自らの生きてきた証さえ見失ってしまったサーシャ。アルフォンもまた、己の存在への疑念の果てに、おそるべき結論にたどり着く。全人類を初期化する重核子爆弾・グランドリバースがもたらす破滅に抗うべく、縁に導かれるかのようにパルチザン艦隊が結集し、切り札である宇宙戦艦アリゾナが飛び立つ。森雪との約束を胸に宇宙戦艦ヤマトの艦長席に座った古代進は、数多の謎の答えと地球の未来を求め、ついにデザリアム本星へと突入する。

2026年製作／103分／G／日本 配給：松竹ODS事業室 劇場公開日：2026年10月30日

{"type": "paragraph", "text": "産業廃棄物の管理型最終処分場となる谷は、廃棄物と土が混ざらないよう地面と縁を切った、大きな鉢のような構造をしている。大きなスペースだが、およそ15年をかけて、廃棄物で埋まっていくという。ただし、この幻想的な光景そのものが作品なのではない。鑑賞者は 西沢立衛 Art Beat"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "次に向かったのは、岡山県倉敷市の 児島ジーンズストリート 。ここは足袋や学生服で培われた裁断・縫製の技術を土台に、日本で初めてジーンズを生み出した「国産ジーンズ発祥の地」だ。約400mの通り沿いに地元メーカーの店舗が約40軒並び、国内外から多くの人が訪れる。歩くだけでも楽しいが、重要文化財・旧野崎家住宅の展示は見逃せない。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "児島ジーンズストリートにて、道路の一部がジーンズの「赤耳」をイメージしている", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "デザインユニット・ SYMBOL PLUS による空間インスタレーション《一粒の布》は、綿花から一着のジーンズへと受け継がれる児島デニムのものづくりがテーマだ。綿花畑を再現した空間に加え、通り沿いの工場やショップを巡るスタンプラリー形式のツアーが用意され、職人の手仕事と、地域に根づくものづくりの文化に触れられる。"}, {"type": "image", "url": {"type": "paragraph", "text": "会場となる旧野崎家住宅は、本芸術祭のほかの会場ともつながりを持つ。創業者の武左衛門は塩田開発のかたわら邸宅の建築にも力を注ぎ、一代で塩田161町歩と大庄屋の広大な屋敷地を築いた。その塩づくりをいまも引き継ぐのが、 ナイカイ塩業 だ。会場をたどるうちに瀬戸内の産業史が見えてくる点も、この芸術祭の見どころになっている。"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "制服の記憶、鉄の心臓、塩の時間"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "長い歴史を持つ工場が続く。玉野市の株式会社トンボは、足袋から学生服へと受け継がれた縫製技術をいまに伝える企業だ。1876年に玉野・八浜で足袋の製造を始め、時代とともに学生服へと事業を移し、創業150年を迎えた国内有数の学生服メーカーである。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/2dcc220a/1e9a22d8-f26e-417e-85f2-996c30fa718e.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "株式会社トンボにて、トンボ学生服のキャラクター「トンボ学」が出迎える", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "制服はたんなる衣服にとどまらず、多くの日本人にとって青春の記憶の器でもある。工場では、資材倉庫から縫製、検品、アイロンまでの製造工程を巡りながら、3人の脚本家によるオーディオドラマ《TOMBOW Voice Theater -制服にまつわる3つの物語-》を聴く。機械の音が響く縫製工程では、制服への愛があふれる《おしゃべりな彼女》（脚本：田中未来）。仕上げ工程では、切なさと温かさが交差する《私と日南》（脚本：三浦直之）。日本中の学校のボタンが保管された資材倉庫では、第二ボタンをめぐる甘酸っぱい物語《心臓に一番近いとこ》（脚本：武田雄樹）が広がる。製造のただなかで進む物語に、気づけば引き込まれている。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/cc544746/76b86f44-2aa7-49b8-96ab-97e55bf78a67.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "株式会社トンボ", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/66048d80/3f602868-2564-4717-b56a-90c1cc8706ec.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "株式会社トンボにて、《TOMBOW Voice Theater -制服にまつわる3つの物語-》展示風景", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "海に面した瀬戸内は、古くから造船が根づく土地でもある。玉野市の三国工業もその産業を支えてきた一社で、大正6年の創業以来、国内シェアトップの舶用大型エンジン部品を中心に、産業機械や鋼構造物まで設計から製作・修理を一貫して行う。本芸術祭でもっとも迫力のある演出が待つのが、この工場だ。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/2dfcfb3c/acc35c67-add3-449c-bb04-33d4ff6e792b.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "MANTLE　船・心臓音・鉄", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat"}, {"type": "paragraph", article_text:
Sponsored by 一般財団法人 日本産業芸術財団

見えにくい産業の魅力を、アートで見せる

製塩、学生服、デニム、造船、蓄電池、資源循環。瀬戸内の暮らしを支えてきた第一次・第二次産業は数多いが、その魅力は外から見えにくい。この課題に取り組むのが、今年初開催の 「瀬戸内産業芸術祭 2026」 である。会期は10月3日から31日まで。

岡山県（岡山市・玉野市・倉敷市）と愛媛県（東温市）の工場・産業現場7会場を舞台に、日本の産業と、それが育んできた文化への理解を深めることを目指す。展示の監修は会場ごとに分かれており、キュレーターの 長谷川祐子 が 大倉佑亮 、 三宅敦大 らとチームを率いて三国工業と藤クリーンの2会場を、建築家の 妹島和世 がオオノ開發を担当する。残るパワーエックス、トンボ、児島ジーンズストリート、ナイカイ塩業の4会場は、全体のキュレーションとブランディングを統括するクリエイティブディレクターの 佐竹正基 が監修する。

作品はすべて事前予約制で、ツアー形式か個別チケットで参加できる。工場見学と鑑賞が一続きになっている点が、一般的な芸術祭との大きな違いだ。

プレスツアーは、愛媛県東温市の オオノ開發 からスタートした。会場は複合リサイクルプラント内の管理型処分場。参加者はまず 増田信吾＋大坪克亘 によるバス停で、 山田紗子 が手がけたマテラカラーの現場服をまとい、バスに乗り込む。この色は、愛媛県産の天然鉱石「マテラパウダー（流紋岩末）」に由来する。約500万㎡の敷地を走る車窓にも、目的地の丘の上にも、橙がかったこの石を見つけることができる。

産業廃棄物の管理型最終処分場となる谷は、廃棄物と土が混ざらないよう地面と縁を切った、大きな鉢のような構造をしている。大きなスペースだが、およそ15年をかけて、廃棄物で埋まっていくという。ただし、この幻想的な光景そのものが作品なのではない。鑑賞者は 西沢立衛 が手がけたマテラカラーの丘に登り、そこから処分場の風景を眺める。自然と人工物、そして人の営みが重なり合う景色を見渡す体験こそが、《最終処分場 -自然と産業、人とつくる風景-》の本題である。

次に向かったのは、岡山県倉敷市の 児島ジーンズストリート 。ここは足袋や学生服で培われた裁断・縫製の技術を土台に、日本で初めてジーンズを生み出した「国産ジーンズ発祥の地」だ。約400mの通り沿いに地元メーカーの店舗が約40軒並び、国内外から多くの人が訪れる。歩くだけでも楽しいが、重要文化財・旧野崎家住宅の展示は見逃せない。

デザインユニット・ SYMBOL PLUS による空間インスタレーション《一粒の布》は、綿花から一着のジーンズへと受け継がれる児島デニムのものづくりがテーマだ。綿花畑を再現した空間に加え、通り沿いの工場やショップを巡るスタンプラリー形式のツアーが用意され、職人の手仕事と、地域に根づくものづくりの文化に触れられる。

会場となる旧野崎家住宅は、本芸術祭のほかの会場ともつながりを持つ。創業者の武左衛門は塩田開発のかたわら邸宅の建築にも力を注ぎ、一代で塩田161町歩と大庄屋の広大な屋敷地を築いた。その塩づくりをいまも引き継ぐのが、 ナイカイ塩業 だ。会場をたどるうちに瀬戸内の産業史が見えてくる点も、この芸術祭の見どころになっている。

制服の記憶、鉄の心臓、塩の時間

長い歴史を持つ工場が続く。玉野市の株式会社トンボは、足袋から学生服へと受け継がれた縫製技術をいまに伝える企業だ。1876年に玉野・八浜で足袋の製造を始め、時代とともに学生服へと事業を移し、創業150年を迎えた国内有数の学生服メーカーである。

制服はたんなる衣服にとどまらず、多くの日本人にとって青春の記憶の器でもある。工場では、資材倉庫から縫製、検品、アイロンまでの製造工程を巡りながら、3人の脚本家によるオーディオドラマ《TOMBOW Voice Theater -制服にまつわる3つの物語-》を聴く。機械の音が響く縫製工程では、制服への愛があふれる《おしゃべりな彼女》（脚本：田中未来）。仕上げ工程では、切なさと温かさが交差する《私と日南》（脚本：三浦直之）。日本中の学校のボタンが保管された資材倉庫では、第二ボタンをめぐる甘酸っぱい物語《心臓に一番近いとこ》（脚本：武田雄樹）が広がる。製造のただなかで進む物語に、気づけば引き込まれている。

海に面した瀬戸内は、古くから造船が根づく土地でもある。玉野市の三国工業もその産業を支えてきた一社で、大正6年の創業以来、国内シェアトップの舶用大型エンジン部品を中心に、産業機械や鋼構造物まで設計から製作・修理を一貫して行う。本芸術祭でもっとも迫力のある演出が待つのが、この工場だ。

伊阪柊と中村壮志によるアートコレクティヴMANTLEの《船・心臓音・鉄》は、作業現場の外から始まる。観客は案内された空間で、工業製品の製造風景や3DCGを用いた映像作品を見る。世界から水がなくなったら？ ある日、謎の巨大なマシンが発見されたら？ 現実とフィクションが混ざり合う物語に耳を傾けたのち、工場の中へ進む。船の心臓にあたる巨大な部品を作る工場には、柱も空間を隔てる壁もなく、溶接や加工の光と音が瞬き、響き渡る。その光景だけでも圧巻だが、奥には映像から飛び出したようなあのマシンが佇んでいる。その姿を撮影することはできないが、重さは約29トン、内部に入ることもできる。私たちの生活を支える工業製品が、どんな未来につながりうるのか。力強い本作がそれを示している。

塩づくりに適した土地という顔も、瀬戸内にはある。岡山・玉野に根ざすナイカイ塩業は、この風土を体現する一社だ。かつての塩田で培われた製法を土台に、余計な殺菌は加えず、自然のままでありながら安全な食塩に仕上げている。

ここで山本基が、同社の塩だけを用いた大規模インスタレーション《たゆたう時》を展開。山本はこれまで、忘れてしまいそうな小さな出来事や大切な人との記憶の積み重ねを、塩の渦として描いてきた。本作ではその渦を「時」に見立て、真っ暗な空間に浮かぶ小さな時の粒として表す。この工場で働く人々の試行錯誤と営み、そして塩がやがて海へ還り、新たな循環へ戻っていく時の連なりに思いを馳せる作品である。

空間演出はSYMBOL PLUSが担い、工場の風景や歴史を再編集した導入空間から、製造ラインを巡るツアーへと続く。撮影禁止のエリアを含むため、ここでしか見られない現場でもある。見学の最後には、同社の塩を使ったアイスクリームの試食が用意されているのも嬉しいポイントだ。

循環と電気のゆくえ

岡山に根ざす藤クリーンは、「廃棄物を資源へ」を掲げる企業だ。産業廃棄物の収集運搬から中間処理、最終処分までを一貫して担い、近年は家庭のプラスチック資源のリサイクルにも取り組む。会場は同社のリサイクルセンターで、これまでも行われてきた見学ツアーに、アーティストのナイル・ケティングとエンジニアのエリオット・エツコーンによるAtmospheric Solutions × Maki Softwareが独自の視点を加える。

《Re: Cycle》は、アプリ、サウンド、学びの要素を重ね、廃棄・再生・循環を多層的な体験として提示するパフォーマティヴ・インスタレーションだ。鑑賞者は専用アプリを手に、施設で扱われるモノの過去・現在・未来を手がかりに、資源が循環していく過程をたどる。オオノ開發とは異なる角度から、日常で使われているものがどうリサイクルされ、どう生まれ変わるのかを知ることができる。アプリに現れる小さなスピリットたちに励まされ、前向きな気持ちで施設をあとにできる作品だ。

そして最後に訪れたのは、次世代エネルギーカンパニーのパワーエックス。日本最大級の蓄電池工場「Power Base」を構え、2025年には本社も玉野市へ移した。系統用大型蓄電池や電気運搬船などの開発を通じて、目に見えない電気を社会に届け、持続可能なエネルギー社会の実現に挑んでいる。

作品は、妹島和世が設計したPower Baseの工場見学ツアーと一体になっている。再生可能エネルギー時代に欠かせない蓄電技術をテーマに、目に見えない「電気」と「調整力」を空間全体で可視化したインスタレーション《調整力》だ。頭上の光は日本各地の発電所を、地面に投影される光は安定した電力を表す。天候によって発電のタイミングが異なるため、発電所の光は明滅するが、地面の光は暗くならない。その間を埋める蓄電池の役割が、光の対比から直感的に伝わってくる。制作を手がけたのは、本芸術祭の展示制作のために発足した、アノニマスの産業芸術家集団SAIだ。

妹島が設計した工場の内部に入れる機会は、普段はほとんどない。このツアーでは、超急速EV充電器や大型蓄電池、生産ラインまで見学できる。建築ファンにとっても、見逃せない機会となるだろう。

廃棄物の最終処分場から縫製工場、舶用エンジン部品工場、製塩所、蓄電池工場まで。7つの現場を巡ると、日々の暮らしが、そこに携わる人々と産業の積み重ねの上に成り立っていることが見えてくる。産業の魅力を知るほどに、作品は現場の文脈を帯びて、違った表情で立ち上がってくるだろう。本芸術祭は今後、全国への展開も目指している。次の舞台がどこになるのか、これからの動きにも注目したい。
